title: Exhaustive search is the only reliable way to find programs with given behavior

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Exhaustive search is the only reliable way to find programs with given behavior

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because simple programs can do so many unexpected things, and computational irreducibility can make finding a behavior take irreducible work, the only reliable way to find a simple program with a desired behavior is essentially exhaustive search, so building a library of basic knowledge about simple programs is a better route to technology.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: ultimately the only way to find what one wants is essentially just to do an exhaustive search of all possibilities.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 12, “The Principle of Computational Equivalence”; section “Implications for Technology” (from p. 840), p. 842. Scope: design of simple programs for technological purposes

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch12-55: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.50

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public synthesis benchmarks can decisively refute restricted versions by demonstrating non-enumerative reliable methods. They cannot establish that exhaustive search is uniquely necessary across all simple-program design problems.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Specify program languages, target-behavior distributions, and resource budgets, then compare exhaustive enumeration against synthesis, gradient, evolutionary, and constraint-based methods. A method that reliably finds targets while skipping most candidates refutes the assertion for that domain.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
"Only reliable way" is a universal quantifier over future algorithms.

Results depend on target and language distributions.

All finite searches can be described as exhaustive over a transformed space.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Program-synthesis and finite-model tools already find some short rules without listing every rule, so the absolute wording can be probed on concrete targets with public software. Computational irreducibility still implies that some targets have no route shorter than a search. A benchmark represents only its suite, so the result tests part of a universal methodological claim.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: On a fixed suite of simple-program targets, compare exhaustive enumeration with constraint solving, heuristic search, and directed mutation, scoring how often each returns a correct short program. A non-exhaustive method that reliably matches the exhaustive search refutes the only-reliable-way reading on that suite.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Worst-case irreducibility can force a search even when typical cases are easy.

Reliable and desired behavior need a benchmark the claim does not state.

Success of a constraint encoding on some targets leaves other targets untouched.
